about.title: Delano Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Kern County recorded two traffic deaths in Delano during the most recent reporting year, alongside 139 injury collisions across corridors like Garces Highway, High Street, County Line Road and Cecil Avenue. Behind each number is a family trying to make sense of a sudden loss, often while facing funeral costs and a home that feels quieter than it should. California law gives surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children the first right to bring a wrongful death claim, with certain other dependents able to step in when no closer relative exists. These cases run on their own civil timeline, separate from anything happening in a criminal court. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we simply help Delano families connect with an independent, contingency-fee attorney who can review what happened, explain the options, and walk beside you through a process that shouldn't be carried alone. There's no obligation, and no fee unless a recovery is made.

whyChoose.title: What Delano Families Should Know About Wrongful Death Claims

items.title: Only Certain Relatives Can File
items.desc: California law limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, then other dependents if none exist. An attorney can help sort out who has standing before any claim moves forward.

items.title: A Firm Two-Year Deadline Applies
items.desc: Wrongful death claims generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter window. Missing either deadline can end a family's ability to recover anything at all.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond the Obvious
items.desc: California allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of love, companionship and guidance — not just tangible expenses. An attorney can help document these losses accurately.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim in Delano depend on the police report or any criminal charges?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action from any criminal case that might follow a fatal crash. A family can pursue a claim whether or not charges are ever filed against the other driver.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: Under California law, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to bring the claim. If none of those relatives exist, certain other dependents or heirs may be eligible instead.

items.question: How long do we have to bring a claim after a crash on a road like Garces Highway or Cecil Avenue?
items.answer: Generally, California gives families two years from the date of death to file. If a government entity, such as a city or county road authority, may bear responsibility, the deadline to act is often much shorter, so it helps to get guidance early.
